context: A uni student interviews a retired bureaucrat about reforms
purpose: Teach: 全文/方策/単一/抜本/内外/明示/明白/さらなる

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただきありがとうございます。当時の改革について、抜本的な見直しに踏み切られた背景を伺いたいのですが。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. I would like to ask about the background behind your decision to undertake fundamental reforms at that time.
lines.style: Polite, earnest interviewer tone with measured pacing and academic curiosity.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、いい質問だね。当時は内外の情勢が大きく変わっていて、従来のやり方ではもう立ち行かないことが明白だったんだよ。
lines.en: Ah, that's a good question. At that time, conditions both at home and abroad were changing greatly, and it was obvious that the old ways could no longer continue.
lines.style: Reflective elderly voice, warm and slightly nostalgic with deliberate pauses.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。具体的にはどのような方策を取られたのでしょうか。資料を読んでも、当時の判断基準が今ひとつ見えてこなくて。
lines.en: I see. What kinds of specific measures did you take? Even reading the documents, the criteria you used at the time aren't quite clear to me.
lines.style: Inquisitive student tone, respectful but probing, slightly hesitant.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: まず方針を明示することから始めたんだ。曖昧なままだと現場が混乱するからね。単一の窓口を設けて、責任の所在をはっきりさせた。
lines.en: We started by clearly stating our policy. If things remain vague, the people on the ground get confused. We set up a single point of contact and clarified where responsibility lay.
lines.style: Patient mentor voice, explanatory and grounded with practical wisdom.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 報告書の全文を拝読しましたが、想像以上に踏み込んだ内容でした。反発はなかったのですか。
lines.en: I read the full text of the report, and the content was bolder than I had imagined. Wasn't there pushback?
lines.style: Impressed but probing, leaning forward conversationally with genuine interest.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: もちろん反発はあったよ。だが、変えなければ立ち行かないことは誰の目にも明白だった。私は逃げずに議論を続けたんだ。
lines.en: Of course there was pushback. But it was clear to everyone that without change, things could not continue. I didn't run from the debate, I kept engaging.
lines.style: Firm conviction with quiet dignity, voice steady and unhurried.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 今後の世代に向けて、さらなる改革が必要だとお考えですか。
lines.en: Do you think further reforms will be necessary for future generations?
lines.style: Earnest closing question, respectful and slightly hopeful in delivery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、必要だね。時代は止まらない。君のような若い人が問い続けてくれることが、何よりの方策だと私は思うよ。
lines.en: Yes, it's necessary. Time doesn't stop. Young people like you continuing to ask questions — that, I think, is the best measure of all.
lines.style: Gentle, encouraging elder tone, passing the torch with warmth.
